== Problem 10 ==

How many integers between 1000 and 9999 have four distinct digits?

<math>\textbf{(A) }3024\qquad\textbf{(B) }4536\qquad\textbf{(C) }5040\qquad\textbf{(D) }6480\qquad \textbf{(E) }6561</math>

==Solution 1==
There are <imath>9</imath> choices for the first number, since it cannot be <imath>0</imath>, there are only <imath>9</imath> choices left for the second number since it must differ from the first, <imath>8</imath> choices for the third number, since it must differ from the first two, and <imath>7</imath> choices for the fourth number, since it must differ from all three.  This means there are <imath>9 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7=\boxed{\textbf{(B) }4536}</imath> integers between <imath>1000</imath> and <imath>9999</imath> with four distinct digits.


If you're too lazy to do <imath>9 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7= 4536</imath>, we can notice <imath> 9 \times 9 = 81</imath> and <imath> 8 \times 7=56</imath> The unit digit must be 6. Therefore, the answer is the only answer choice with a unit digit of 6, which is <imath>\boxed{B}</imath>.
